title: Interception of highly sensitive registration data in transit
description: The parent sends email, password, name, government ID, and a six-digit code to the Authentication Service. If the flow is not strongly protected in transit, an attacker observing the channel could learn directly identifying and credential data.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection is absent, weak, misconfigured, or can be bypassed on some client/network paths.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types for ExternalEntity->Process flows but not detailed subtree ids.

title: Excessive identifiability from combined registration attributes
description: This single registration flow contains multiple strong identifiers and authenticators together: email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code. Their combination makes the parent directly identifiable to the Authentication Service and to any party that gains access to the flow contents.
assumptions: Assumes the service can associate these attributes with one account or person record.
uncertainty_note: Identifiability is inherent to the data content of the flow; exact subtree id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Over-disclosure of personal data during registration
description: The registration flow includes government ID in addition to email, name, password, and code. If government ID is not strictly necessary at account creation, the flow discloses more personal data than needed for the stated purpose of authentication/registration.
assumptions: Assumes government ID is not essential for initial registration or could be collected later or via a more privacy-preserving verification step.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on business necessity for collecting government ID at registration time.

title: Unawareness about collection and use of sensitive identity data
description: A parent may not be adequately informed, at the moment of this flow, why government ID and the six-digit code are required, how they will be verified, retained, shared, or whether they are mandatory. This creates a risk that the user submits sensitive data without sufficient understanding.
assumptions: Assumes the registration interface or notice may not clearly explain purpose, retention, recipients, and optionality for each field.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible flow-level privacy threat, but confirmation would require UI/notice details not present in the DFD.

title: Collection may exceed consent or legal basis expectations
description: Collecting government ID and other registration data in one step may go beyond what the parent reasonably expects for creating an account, especially if explicit consent, necessity, or another valid legal basis is not clearly established for each attribute.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on consent or another legal basis that may not be properly scoped or communicated for all collected fields.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on jurisdiction, purpose specification, and the actual legal basis used by the service.

title: Parent can later dispute having submitted registration details
description: If the system does not create appropriate evidence of the registration submission and associated notices, the parent may later deny having provided the email, government ID, or code, or deny having agreed to the registration step under the presented terms.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient logging, timestamping, notice versioning, or proof of submission.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is applicable to this interaction type per mapping, but whether it is a material privacy issue depends on evidencing and accountability requirements.

title: Excessive storage of parent account personal data
description: The flow stores a parent account in the users collection. If the stored record contains more personal data than is strictly necessary for authentication/account management, the datastore becomes a point of avoidable disclosure because unnecessary personal data is retained and accessible within the system.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account record may include profile, contact, relationship, or other attributes beyond the minimum needed to create and maintain the account.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for a data-minimisation / unnecessary storage disclosure case; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->DataStore flows but does not provide the exact subtree citation.

title: Unauthorised modification of stored parent account data
description: When the authentication service writes parent account data to the users collection, insufficient integrity protection on this flow or at the datastore could allow account attributes to be altered, leading to incorrect personal data being stored about the parent.
assumptions: Assumes missing or weak write validation, transaction controls, or access restrictions on writes into the users collection.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subtree id is inferred from general integrity threats; retrieved context only establishes that Integrity applies at Process->DataStore flows.

title: Lack of evidence for who stored or changed the parent account
description: If the write of the parent account into MongoDB is not logged with sufficient provenance, the system may be unable to prove which process instance or actor created or modified the stored personal data. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant actions on the account record.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging for create/update operations is absent, incomplete, or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; applicability of non-repudiation to this storage flow is strong, but the retrieved context does not include the detailed threat tree.

title: Insufficient transparency about storage of parent account data
description: The flow persists parent account data in the users collection. If users are not informed that their data is stored, what fields are stored, for how long, and for what purposes, the storage operation can create a detectability/awareness issue around the existence and handling of their personal data.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-product explanations do not clearly disclose this storage activity.
uncertainty_note: This is included as a detectability/awareness-related privacy threat, but the exact fit between classic LINDDUN detectability and transparency wording may vary by interpretation.

title: Secondary use of stored parent account data beyond authentication
description: Once parent account data is stored in the users collection, it may later be used for purposes beyond the original authentication/account-creation purpose, such as analytics, profiling, or cross-feature reuse, without a compatible legal basis or user expectation.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation is not technically or organisationally enforced for records in the users collection.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is inferred; the threat is grounded in foreseeable misuse of stored data after collection rather than the write operation alone.

title: Storage of parent account data without a valid legal basis or consent handling
description: If the parent account is stored in MongoDB without establishing and recording the appropriate legal basis, consent state, parental relationship basis, or retention obligations, the storage operation may violate applicable privacy requirements.
assumptions: Assumes this account data includes personal data subject to consent, contract, legitimate-interest balancing, child/parent relationship verification, or retention constraints.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; non-compliance applicability depends on jurisdiction and the specific account fields stored.

title: JWT and returned user data can enable cross-context linkability
description: The authentication response contains a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the JWT contains stable identifiers or correlatable claims, or if the returned user data includes persistent account attributes, the parent user or intermediaries can link multiple sessions, devices, or service interactions belonging to the same data subject.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT includes stable subject identifiers, account IDs, or other persistent claims, and/or the user data contains identifying attributes reused across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement because the retrieved context only gives applicable threat types, not detailed node mappings for this specific flow.

title: Authentication response may disclose excessive identity information
description: Sending a JWT plus user data to the parent user may reveal more personal information than is necessary for the immediate authentication purpose. JWT claims or bundled profile data could expose identifiers, roles, contact details, family relationships, or other attributes to the recipient or to parties able to observe the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the token or accompanying user data contains personal attributes beyond a minimal authentication assertion.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node is approximate; the core issue is disclosure of personal data in the flow.

title: Lack of proof about what authentication data was released
description: If the authentication service does not keep adequate records of which JWT claims and user data were sent to the parent user, it may be impossible later to demonstrate what personal data was disclosed, when it was disclosed, and under which legal or business basis. This can hinder dispute resolution and accountability.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient audit logging or non-repudiation controls around issuance and delivery of tokens and profile data.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if the system lacks reliable issuance/disclosure logs.

title: JWT and user data may be detectable in transit or through metadata
description: Even if the payload is protected, the existence, timing, size, and frequency of authentication responses to the parent user can reveal that a specific user is logging in or accessing the service. If transport protection is weak or terminated at intermediaries, the JWT and user data themselves may also become observable.
assumptions: Assumes network observers, browser extensions, reverse proxies, or other intermediaries may access traffic metadata or content.
uncertainty_note: Exact node is approximate; detectability here concerns observability of the authentication event and possibly its contents.

title: Returned token and profile data may enable identification beyond necessity
description: A JWT commonly carries a subject identifier and may include email, username, role, or other claims. Combined with returned user data, this can directly identify the data subject to the parent user or any party obtaining the response, even where a less identifying assertion would suffice.
assumptions: Assumes the response includes direct or quasi-identifiers rather than a privacy-preserving, minimal token.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement due to lack of detailed node mapping in the retrieved context.

title: Parent user may be unaware of JWT contents and downstream uses
description: The parent user may not understand what personal data is embedded in the JWT or accompanying user data, how long the token remains valid, which relying components can read it, or for what secondary purposes the data may be used. This undermines transparency and informed expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly explain token contents, recipients, retention, and usage to the parent user.
uncertainty_note: This is a transparency/unawareness threat contingent on insufficient notice or explanation.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation requirements
description: Providing a JWT together with user data to the parent user may exceed what is necessary for authentication if the flow includes unnecessary claims or profile attributes. This can create non-compliance with privacy requirements such as data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or lawful-basis constraints.
assumptions: Assumes the implementation returns more claims or user attributes than strictly needed for the parent user's purpose.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction, applicable policy, and the exact claims/attributes included in the response.

title: Login submission can be linked to the child across sessions via stable parent email
description: The flow carries a stable identifier (parent email) together with authentication data. Reuse of the same email on each login enables the authentication service and any observer of the flow to link repeated login attempts and build a longitudinal profile of the child account usage.
assumptions: The parent email is persistent and uniquely associated with the child's account or household.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement for linkability on a data flow; exact node numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent email directly identifies the child account or household
description: The login flow includes the parent's email address, which is a direct identifier for the household and may also uniquely identify the child's account. Anyone with access to the flow content can identify which family is attempting to authenticate.
assumptions: The email address is unique within the service and visible in plaintext to the receiving process and potentially intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifiability node id is based on best judgement; the applicability of identifiability itself is strong.

title: Login credentials disclose sensitive personal data in transit
description: The flow contains authentication secrets (password) and personal data (parent email). If the transmission channel, client environment, logs, or intermediaries are insufficiently protected, these data may be exposed beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Threat concerns the privacy exposure on this flow, not broader account compromise impacts.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure node id may differ across threat-tree editions; disclosure on the flow clearly applies.

title: Child may be unaware that parent email is used as the login identifier
description: Because the child login uses the parent's email and password, the child may not understand which personal data are being transmitted and how this ties the child's use of the service to the parent or household. This creates a risk of insufficient transparency about the processing triggered by login.
assumptions: The service is used by children and transparency notices may not be presented in a child-understandable way at login time.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is inferred from the child-user context and may depend on UI and notice design not shown in the DFD.

title: Collection of parent email for child authentication may exceed data-minimization expectations
description: Using a parent's email address as part of a child's login may process personal data of both child and parent. If this identifier is not strictly necessary for authentication, the flow may create a non-compliance risk with data-minimization, purpose-limitation, or children's privacy requirements.
assumptions: Alternative less identifying authentication mechanisms may be feasible; child-specific regulatory obligations may apply.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction, age group, and service design; threat is plausible but context-dependent.

title: JWT and child profiles enable linkability across sessions and services
description: The authentication service sends a JWT identifying the user as a child together with child profile data. If the JWT contains a stable subject, account identifier, or other persistent claims, the child can be linked across sessions and potentially across relying services that receive or inspect the token, allowing correlation of the same child over time.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifiers or correlatable claims and may be reused across sessions or presented to multiple components/services.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; exact subnode may vary depending on the project’s LINDDUN Pro threat tree version.

title: JWT and profile payload may reveal identifying information about a child
description: Delivering a JWT plus child profiles to the child user may expose identifiers or quasi-identifiers such as account id, username, age band, avatar, preferences, household relationships, or other profile attributes. If the token or profile data is observable by unintended parties on the device, in logs, browser storage, or via interception, it can identify the child.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT/profile contains personal data and that client-side exposure or interception is possible.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifying fields are not listed in the flow description, so this is based on the common contents of JWTs and profile payloads.

title: Authentication response discloses child status and profile attributes beyond necessity
description: The response explicitly includes userType=child and child profiles. This reveals that the authenticated user is a child and may disclose additional profile attributes that are not strictly necessary for the immediate authentication step, increasing exposure of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Assumes some profile fields are not strictly required to complete authentication and could be minimized or deferred.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the precise disclosure subnode depends on the threat-tree taxonomy version.

title: Child user may be unaware of token claims and profile data shared in the authentication response
description: The flow returns a JWT and child profiles, but the child user may not be informed what claims are embedded in the token, how long it remains valid, where it will be stored, or which profile attributes are being sent and later reused. This creates a risk of insufficient data transparency.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain token contents, retention, recipients, and purposes in a child-appropriate manner.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency notices are absent or not understandable for children; this cannot be confirmed from the flow alone.

title: JWT and child profiles may be used for purposes beyond authentication
description: Combining an authentication token with child profile data creates a risk that the data will later be used for personalization, analytics, tracking, or access decisions beyond the original login purpose. Without strict purpose limitation, the child’s data may be processed in ways not expected from an authentication exchange.
assumptions: Assumes downstream components can access or reuse the JWT claims/profile data for secondary purposes.
uncertainty_note: Secondary use is a plausible risk from this flow, but actual downstream reuse is not shown in the DFD snippet.

title: Sending child profiles in the authentication response may violate data minimization and child-data compliance requirements
description: Returning both a JWT and child profiles in one authentication flow may exceed what is necessary for login, especially for a child account. If unnecessary profile attributes are included, or if child-specific legal requirements for transparency, minimization, parental authorization, or retention are not met, the flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child-privacy obligations exist and that some profile data may be unnecessary at this stage.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction and actual profile fields; exact legal obligations are outside the flow description.

title: Child profile attributes can be linked into a uniquely identifying profile
description: The flow sends a combination of name, date of birth, gender, and government ID from the parent to Child Profile Management. This attribute set is highly linkable and enables the process to associate records across sessions, services, or datasets, creating a persistent child profile and potentially revealing additional information through correlation.
assumptions: Assumes the process stores or reuses these attributes, especially the government ID, as stable identifiers for the child profile.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context confirms Linking applicability for ExternalEntity->Process flows but does not provide the detailed threat-tree node list.

title: Child identity can be directly identified from submitted profile data
description: The submitted data contains direct identifiers and strong quasi-identifiers, notably name and government ID, plus date of birth and gender. On receipt by Child Profile Management, the child is identifiable rather than merely pseudonymous, increasing privacy risk if the data is exposed, reused, or combined with other records.
assumptions: Assumes the government ID and name correspond to the child and are processed as part of account/profile creation.
uncertainty_note: Detailed tree-node citation is approximate; applicability of Identifiability to this flow is strong.

title: Excessive collection of sensitive child profile data enables unnecessary disclosure
description: This flow collects a broad set of personal data for profile creation, including government ID and date of birth. If all fields are not strictly necessary for the stated purpose, the process receives more personal data than needed, increasing the impact of accidental exposure, internal misuse, or secondary use.
assumptions: Assumes necessity and proportionality of each field have not yet been justified; government ID is often especially sensitive for routine profile creation.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded in disclosure/data minimization concerns at the receiving process; exact node id is approximate.

title: Collection of child data may lack clear necessity, consent basis, or parental transparency
description: The flow involves creation of a child profile using sensitive identifying attributes. If Child Profile Management does not provide clear notice, lawful basis, parental authorization handling, retention information, and purpose limitation for each field, the collection may be non-compliant with child-data protection requirements and data minimization obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy regulation and that child data requires heightened protections and transparency.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and actual notices/consent mechanisms, which are not provided here; node id is best judgement.

title: Excessive child-profile data stored in childprofiles collection
description: The flow stores or updates a child profile in persistent storage. If the profile contains more personal data than is strictly necessary for the service purpose, or retains optional/sensitive child attributes by default, the datastore creates an avoidable explicit disclosure risk because personal data is collected and stored beyond data-minimization needs.
assumptions: Child profiles may include directly identifying, demographic, behavioral, or other sensitive child-related attributes; persistent storage increases exposure duration.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgment for a data-disclosure/minimization threat because the retrieved context gives threat-type applicability but not the detailed Dd subtree for this exact case.

title: Unauthorized modification of stored child profiles
description: Because this flow updates records in the childprofiles collection, insufficient integrity controls on write operations could allow unauthorized or accidental alteration of a child's profile data. This can lead to incorrect personal data being stored and subsequently used in decisions or downstream processing about the child.
assumptions: The flow supports both create and update operations and may be reachable by multiple internal components or roles.
uncertainty_note: Applicable to a write flow, but the exact LINDDUN Pro integrity subtree node may differ; node id is approximate.

title: Lack of auditable proof for child-profile changes
description: If writes to the childprofiles collection are not logged with actor, timestamp, and change details, the system may be unable to prove who created or modified a child's profile. This undermines accountability for privacy-relevant changes and hampers dispute resolution, consent tracing, or incident investigation.
assumptions: Profile updates may affect privacy rights, parental controls, or service behavior and therefore require accountability.
uncertainty_note: Threat is plausible for update flows, but exact subtree citation is approximate because detailed Nr nodes were not provided in context.

title: Unclear purpose or consequences of storing child-profile attributes
description: The flow persists child-profile information, but if users or guardians are not clearly informed which attributes are stored, why they are needed, and how updates affect the child's account or experience, data subjects may be unaware of the processing. This creates an unawareness threat tied to the storage/update operation.
assumptions: Some profile fields may be entered or inferred without sufficiently clear notices or just-in-time explanations.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded in the privacy transparency aspect of storing child data, but the exact U subtree node is approximate.

title: Storage of child-profile data without a valid legal basis or policy constraint
description: Persisting or updating child-profile records may violate privacy obligations if the system stores fields without an appropriate legal basis, parental authorization where required, age-related safeguards, or retention/purpose constraints. The datastore then contains personal data processed outside applicable policy or regulatory requirements.
assumptions: The application may process children's data, which often triggers stricter compliance obligations than adult data.
uncertainty_note: Compliance risk is genuine for child-profile storage, but the exact Nc subtree node is approximate due to missing detailed tree context.

title: Search, like, and comment requests can be linked to the same child profile
description: Repeated video searches, requests, likes, and comments sent from the child user to the video management service may carry stable account, device, session, or network identifiers. This enables the service to link multiple actions over time into a behavioral profile of the child.
assumptions: Assumes the flow contains or is accompanied by persistent identifiers such as account ID, cookie, device ID, IP address, or authenticated session context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context confirms L applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows but did not include the detailed L threat-tree node list.

title: Interaction content reveals child interests and preferences
description: Video search terms, requested videos, likes, and comments can reveal the child's interests, habits, emotional state, opinions, or other personal characteristics. Even if explicit profile fields are absent, the content of this flow may disclose sensitive inferences about the child.
assumptions: Assumes search queries, requested content identifiers, likes, or free-text comments are visible to the receiving service.
uncertainty_note: Detailed I-node citation is approximate; applicability of information disclosure to this flow is strong.

title: Insufficient evidence of child actions may undermine contestability
description: If the video management service does not keep trustworthy records of submitted searches, requests, likes, or comments, it may be unable to prove what action was performed, when, and under which account or session. This can hinder dispute resolution, parental review, or correction when harmful or unintended interactions occur.
assumptions: Assumes the service relies on this flow for moderation, parental controls, or account history, but logging or integrity protections may be weak.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation in privacy is context-dependent here; included because user-generated interactions often require later contestability and accountability.

title: Search and engagement actions are detectable by the service and observers
description: The act of sending video searches, requests, likes, and comments is itself observable by the receiving service and potentially by network observers if transport protection is inadequate. This makes the child's activity detectable even before considering the detailed content.
assumptions: Assumes the flow occurs over a channel where the service can observe timing and occurrence, and possibly intermediaries can too if metadata is exposed.
uncertainty_note: Specific D-node is selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not provide detailed detectability tree nodes.

title: Traffic and interaction patterns may disclose viewing behavior
description: Even where message payloads are minimized, the frequency, timing, and sequence of searches, requests, likes, and comments can disclose when and how intensely a child engages with videos. Such metadata can reveal routines, preferences, or reactions to content.
assumptions: Assumes metadata such as timestamps, request frequency, and action sequence are available to the service or other observers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is approximate; threat is grounded in disclosure through metadata rather than payload content.

title: Child may be unaware of profiling from search and engagement inputs
description: A child user may not understand that searches, requests, likes, and comments are collected and used to personalize recommendations, moderate content, or build engagement profiles. This creates a risk that the child cannot make an informed decision about participating in the interaction.
assumptions: Assumes notices are absent, unclear, not age-appropriate, or not presented at the point of collection.
uncertainty_note: Detailed unawareness node is approximate; the general threat is strongly applicable for child-directed interactions.

title: Collection and use of child interaction data may be non-compliant
description: Processing a child's video searches, requests, likes, and comments may violate child-privacy, consent, transparency, retention, or purpose-limitation obligations if the service collects more data than necessary, uses it for profiling or advertising, or lacks appropriate parental authorization and safeguards.
assumptions: Assumes the child is subject to heightened legal protection and the service may use this flow for analytics, personalization, moderation, or marketing.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 is directly supported by retrieved context, but the exact legal non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and actual controls.

title: Identified information in stored video metadata
description: The videos collection may store metadata that directly identifies a person, such as uploader/account identifiers, names, email-linked account references, or other identifying tags associated with a video record. Because this flow persists metadata into the datastore, identified information can become attached to each stored item and enable direct identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes video metadata includes user/account identifiers or other directly identifying fields, which is common for video-management services.

title: Excessive storage of personal data in video files and metadata
description: This flow stores video files and metadata in the database layer. Video content can contain personal data about data subjects, and metadata may include additional personal details. If the service stores more content or metadata than is strictly necessary for the stated purpose, the datastore creates an avoidable data-disclosure risk through over-collection and over-retention of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes uploaded videos may depict identifiable individuals and that metadata may include personal attributes beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement from LINDDUN Data Disclosure/minimality guidance; exact subnode citation was not present in the retrieved context.

title: Linkability across video records via persistent identifiers
description: Persisting video metadata in a central collection can allow multiple records to be linked to the same uploader, channel, device, IP-derived source, or other stable identifier. This enables correlation of separate uploads or accesses and may reveal behavioral patterns about a person across videos.
assumptions: Assumes the stored metadata contains stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers reused across records.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode may vary depending on the specific identifier used; node chosen by best judgement.

title: Detectability of a person's presence from stored video metadata
description: Even if full video content is not exposed, the existence of a record in the videos collection and its metadata may allow an observer with access to the datastore or derived outputs to detect that a particular person uploaded, appeared in, or is associated with a video. Record existence, timestamps, titles, tags, or ownership fields can make a subject's involvement detectable.
assumptions: Assumes metadata includes fields from which a person's association with a video can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Exact D threat-tree subnode not provided in retrieved context; selected by best judgement.

title: Storage of video data without clear purpose limitation or retention constraints
description: This flow writes video files and metadata into persistent storage. If the system lacks clear purpose limitation, retention periods, or lawful-basis constraints for these stored data, the processing may become non-compliant with privacy obligations because personal data in videos is typically sensitive in scope and duration.
assumptions: Assumes the design has not yet demonstrated explicit retention, deletion, or purpose-limitation controls for stored videos and metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subnode is based on general LINDDUN non-compliance reasoning rather than a retrieved citation.

title: Excessive retention of child search and watch history
description: Storing detailed child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for the service purpose. Such histories can reveal interests, habits, routines, and potentially sensitive inferences about a child, so retaining full event-level history creates an avoidable data disclosure risk if minimization and retention limits are not applied.
assumptions: Assumes the collection stores identifiable or reasonably linkable child-level history rather than only short-lived aggregated telemetry, and that full history is persisted beyond immediate operational need.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is based on best judgment for a minimization/storage-related data disclosure threat; exact node labeling may vary across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Stored history enables identification of a child profile
description: Persisting search and watch history in a profile-linked datastore can make an individual child identifiable, especially when combined with account, device, or household context. Even if direct identifiers are limited, unique viewing and search patterns may single out a child profile.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with a persistent child profile or other stable identifier in the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is chosen by best judgment because the retrieved context did not include the detailed identity threat tree.

title: Cross-session linkability through persistent history storage
description: A persistent childprofiles collection storing search and watch history allows events from multiple sessions to be linked to the same child profile. This enables construction of a longitudinal behavior record, increasing privacy risk beyond a single interaction.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore uses a stable profile key or equivalent persistent reference across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is based on best judgment for linkability via persistent identifiers/history.

title: Behavioral profiling from stored child activity history
description: Detailed search and watch history can be used to infer a child's preferences, interests, age-related traits, routines, or other characteristics. This creates a detectability/inference risk because observers or internal analytics can detect sensitive patterns from the stored data.
assumptions: Assumes the stored history is sufficiently granular to support behavioral analysis or pattern detection.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-judgment mapping to a detectability/inference-oriented node; some methodologies might classify parts of this concern under disclosure or linkability instead.

title: Potential non-compliance with children's data minimization and retention obligations
description: Storing child search and watch history may conflict with privacy obligations if the system lacks a clear lawful basis, age-appropriate transparency, strict purpose limitation, or retention controls. Because the data concerns children, regulatory expectations for necessity and protection are heightened.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to child-privacy or general data-protection requirements and that compliance controls are not yet demonstrated for this storage flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is selected by best judgment; compliance applicability depends on jurisdiction and implemented controls.

title: Uploaded video and metadata may enable identification of the child or family
description: The uploaded video, together with approval/rejection context and associated account metadata, can directly or indirectly identify the child, parent, household, school, or location if the service processes or exposes recognizable faces, voices, surroundings, filenames, timestamps, or uploader identifiers beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes the uploaded content contains personal data and that the service stores or makes it accessible to staff, moderators, or downstream components.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement; the retrieved context did not include the specific Identifiability subtree.

title: Video upload may disclose sensitive personal data to unauthorized parties
description: A video upload can contain extensive personal and potentially special-category data about a child and family. If the Video Management Service lacks strict access control, secure transmission handling, or segregation during approval/rejection workflows, the content and decision status may be disclosed to unauthorized internal users, processors, or external attackers.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries the video itself and related decision metadata, and that multiple actors or systems may access the service during moderation.
uncertainty_note: Specific disclosure subtree node is inferred from general LINDDUN knowledge because the retrieved context did not provide D threat-tree details.

title: Parent may be unaware of how uploaded videos are used in approval/rejection processing
description: If the service does not clearly explain who reviews uploads, what criteria drive approval or rejection, how long videos are retained, whether automated analysis is used, and whether content is reused for training, moderation, or sharing, the parent may lack sufficient awareness and transparency regarding processing of personal data in this flow.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or just-in-time explanations may be incomplete for the upload workflow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; the retrieved context did not include the Unawareness subtree.

title: Approval/rejection workflow may process children's video data without proper compliance controls
description: The service may collect and process children's video data without adequate lawful basis, parental authorization checks, purpose limitation, retention limits, or records supporting data subject rights. This creates non-compliance risk in the upload and moderation flow, especially given the sensitivity of minors' audiovisual data.
